title: Agents at Scale: Inside MiniMax's Model and the Infrastructure Behind It — Dan Fu and Olive Song
talk_summary: Panel with MiniMax's RL lead and Together AI's inference VP covers open-weight model launch, multimodal/long-horizon RL training, and inference optimization for agentic workloads. Most content is model-serving specific; transferable bits are workload-aware context/caching, long-run checkpoint evaluation with anti-hacking validation, and internal evals derived from real work.

takeaways.technique: Internal evals derived from real work
takeaways.what_they_do: They use the model to speed internal development and then turn that work into evaluations closely related to their own tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can build our own evaluations that are closely related to our own work

takeaways.technique: Checkpointed long-run eval with anti-hack validators
takeaways.what_they_do: For long-horizon tasks they let the model submit multiple times, evaluate each submission, and use validation/tests to distinguish real improvement from hacking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do do like validation and test with for it to test if it's really improving on the performance or it's hacking

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat coding-agent workloads with whole-codebase context as a different KV-cache, prompting, and routing problem than chat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with the coding base agentic workflows, you'll upload your whole code base to the model, and that's a very different optimization and routing and kernel challenge

takeaways.what_they_do: They let agentic turn-based workload shape inform KV cache, prompting, and which part of the stack to optimize.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these agentic turn-based workloads, they go into everything from informing your KV cash, your prompting

takeaways.what_they_do: They design long-horizon RL environments around hardware constraints and reward formulation rather than treating the task as pure prompting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the task itself would require GPUs. It has hardware constraints.
